matches.description: Watch Slovenia vs Scotland highlights and goals from UEFA Nations League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on September 26, 2026. The atmosphere was thick with anticipation as Slovenia and Scotland squared off in a high-stakes UEFA Nations League encounter. On September 26, 2026, both sides took to the pitch looking to claim dominance in a match defined by tactical discipline and defensive resilience. A Tactical Standoff in the Opening Half The contest began with Slovenia looking to exploit set-piece opportunities. Early corners from David Brekalo and Danijel Sturm tested the Scottish resolve, but the visiting defense remained organized. Andraz Sporar was a focal point for the hosts, though he struggled with his clinical edge, twice missing the target and being flagged offside during a cagey first forty-five minutes. The tension boiled over late in the half when Scotland's captain Andrew Robertson received a yellow card for unsportsmanlike conduct. Scotland gradually asserted their authority through superior ball retention. John McGinn was central to their efforts, seeing a goalbound effort blocked by a sliding Slovenian defender. Despite controlling much of the tempo, the Scots found it difficult to break through a compact home side that prioritized defensive structure over expansive play. Hendry Denied by Goal-Line Heroics The second half saw the visitors ramp up the pressure, eventually finishing the match with a dominant 65% of possession. The defining moment arrived in the 65th minute when Jack Hendry unleashed a strike that seemed destined for the net, only for a Slovenian defender to heroically hack the ball off the goal line. It was a massive let-off for the hosts and a moment of pure frustration for the Tartan Army. Both goalkeepers were forced into action as the game stretched. Jan Oblak produced a comfortable but vital save to deny an Oli McBurnie header, while at the other end, Angus Gunn stood tall to catch a dangerous cross in the dying embers of the game. Substitutions from both managers, including the introduction of Kieron Bowie for Scotland and Sandi Lovric for Slovenia, failed to provide the clinical touch required to break the deadlock. Discipline Fades in the Final Minutes As the clock ticked toward full-time, the physicality of the match increased. Adam Gnezda Cerin was booked for dissent, followed shortly by yellow cards for Zan Karnicnik and Sandi Lovric as they attempted to halt Scottish breaks. Despite a late flurry of activity in the Slovenian box and a blocked effort from Andrew Robertson , the match ended 0-0. It was a night of missed opportunities for Scotland and defensive pride for the 12,182 fans in attendance.
